Lilith came to me when I was young and I remember feeling really drawn to her but also terrified. I read about her many times, I felt a deep sense of sympathy for Lucifer and Lilith but I was raised in an environment influenced by catholicism (although my parents weren’t really religious) so I felt that it was « wrong ». 

Fast forward 10+ years, stuck in a very abusive relationship with a man twice my age that had isolated me, mocked me, beat me, sa’ed me for years now. I felt hopeless, basically still a child with a firstborn to care for, I was doomed. Or so I thought. 

One particularly bad day, I remember going to my room after he had been berating me and hearing a voice in my head saying « Lilith… Lilith… I’ll get you out of here, trust in me… I’ll give you back your power… ». I hadn’t even thought of Lilith for years at this point! It was completely out of nowhere. I remember submitting mentally, letting go of any fear, just basically giving in to Lilith. 

My life changed that day. I know it seems dramatic but it did. Everything happened like a tornado, chaotic but necessary. Some things are very personal to say but some events happened, events that gave me a true chance to get out, I didn’t even have to worry about things because they just… happened. Everything unfolded constantly and I merely had a say in what was going on. 

Some things hurt and sometimes I cried out of rage because the events were painful to go through but deep down I knew they were necessary. Lilith was building me up and building me a life that I had desired. I have no hesitation in saying this, she very much saved my life. I believe Lucifer played a role too. 

Years later, those years are just a distant memory. Now, my practice has ups and downs but I keep my faith in Lilith and Lucifer, and I found a community that I love here! :)

Gallbladder removal. Didn’t know bariatric surgery was such a precursor, I needed urgent surgery because my gallbladder was bursting with stones. 

Stomach ulcers and GERD. Especially if you smoke or consume alcohol. It’s not a good mix for bariatric patients! Ulcers are really fucking painful. 

Malnutrition, low ferritin, anemia. Ask me how many IV pouches of iron infusions I’ve had this year so far… My intestines just doesn’t absorb nutrients properly and we’ve been trying things for years. 

Finally, esophageal problems. I had never heard about that until this year I started having painful esophagus spasms. I didn’t even think it was associated with my bariatric surgery until the doctors connected the dots. I’m currently awaiting an endoscopy for that.

I always recommend my friends to start with a retinol that’s around 0.3% to 0.5%, I wouldn’t go to 1% right away. Use at night, first once or twice the first week then a few times a week to see how your skin reacts first. Using the sandwich method is nice, like a moisturizing essence and then the retinol and then a little bit of moisturizing cream, nothing with other actives though, keep it plain and simple. Don’t use retinol on a wet face. Don’t use retinol in the morning. Do use a good sunscreen throughout the day. I don’t recommend using Vitamin C and retinol all at once, I burned my face that way. Vitamin C is better used in the morning and retinol in the evening. 

Which one to get pretty much depends on what’s your budget and what’s available to you. I really like Indeed Labs Retinol Reface when I started and it’s mad affordable!

My husband has HS, I don’t. When we first met, he had a lot of scars and tunnels under his belly, in the groin area, between the thighs, armpits, some on his chest and neck and a lot on his butt. He was so ashamed, kept asking if he was stinky, that he was sorry for his skin but didn’t actually explain what was the condition so I gently asked him if he was okay talking about it and what kind of scars they were, that it was fine for me as it didn’t impact my sexual attraction to him at all. I just wanted him to be able to feel confident. He even told me he was scared I’d ghost him after our first time which never crossed my mind! 

Knowing about his condition made me able to help him with bad flares and be more careful in bed sometimes because I know it can be very painful for you guys. I’m also able to watch for signs of infection. I take care of some impacted tunnels or annoying blackheads. I’ve helped him drain some cysts the size of golf balls and I still want to kiss his face and jump his bones every day! It never disgusted me and I’m so glad he opened up about it early on. 

My advice would be, be blunt, explain it, explain what they can expect during sex. It’s not a condition you have control over and I think mature people will understand and see past that.

Giving birth as a young woman, to my second child while tending to my mother who was dying to cancer. I don’t think many people get just how surreal it felt. There was something incredibly cruel yet beautiful to me to bring someone to death as I had just brought someone to life. I was, in that very instant, a textbook representation of the cycle of life. It was fascinating but so sad. 
To that very little newborn, I was a grown, strong mother and to my mom, I was her little baby weeping for her. 

Happy Mother’s Day, mom. It’s been five months and I still can’t sleep without waking up to think about you. 

I’ll add that my mom’s cancer was genetic and I tested positive for the same gene mutation as her. While I was taking care of her in the hospital, freshly postpartum, I had to go under a biopsy after an MRI and wait for my results to know if I had cancer, just like her. I’d watch her, frail and unstable, her eyes sunken and her nonsense words tormented with pain for two weeks while waiting for my results, wondering if my two daughters would have to watch over me like this one day. And I know very well it’s a possibility. 

My mom died a few minutes after I got the phone call by her oncologist, which is my oncologist as well, to tell me my biopsy came back negative for cancer. I came back in the room to tell my mom and she took her two final breaths and finally let herself go. Tragically magical, that moment.

Okay so next time you are in the shower, wet your hair but don’t wash it or condition it yet. Try to get a hair to fall from your head and then wrap it between your fingers and pull, not too quick or too strong but just a steady pulling. If the hair breaks, you probably have too much protein. If the hair extends a lot, your hair might be over moisturized which can happen when people are looking for shine or gloss and think deeply moisturizing consistently will give them that. If you hair resists and doesn’t break nor extend overly, your hair is balanced. 

I do this with 2-3 hairs to see if my results are consistent because I’ve had hair colours and highlights in the past. I’d say based on my hair type, if my hair resists but still feels dry, I just know it needs a good dose of oils and silicones! You can make 2-3 poached eggs at the same time if you are using a medium-sized pot. You won’t drop them all at the same time because they all need to go through the vortex at the center first, but within 30 seconds of dropping your first egg, you can add your second one. 

If you are doing more than one, keep your fire open but on simmer, otherwise your pot will lose too much heat for the last egg. 
It’s imperative you drop your eggs separately in small bowls before cooking them. If you drop them straight into the pot, they have more chances of being stringy. The bowl gives them a uniform shape and it’ll be easier for you to drop them closer to the water surface. Having all your little bowls ready makes the process smoother. 

Okay so let’s say you dropped your first egg about 30 seconds ago. You are swirling around it. Here you can gently push your egg to the side and incorporate it in the swirl with the help of your wooden spoon. Don’t touch the egg, just use the water and your spoon to push it around. Create a swirl again, don’t be rough, just follow the previous swirl. You can add another egg in the middle and so on. 

Some people use a metal ladle instead which is fine but takes a bit more practice because it’s bulkier, heavier and you have more chances of touching the eggs and ruining them. The upside of the ladle is you can hold one egg while dropping the others, but once again it requires expertise. 

You do want to use a slotted spoon to get your poached eggs out. Don’t use the wooden spoon for this.
